clue.text: West Indian works underneath water pump?

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
IND is a standard abbreviation for Indian
a mill is a works or factory

explanation.surface: A Caribbean factory sits below a water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' looks like one idea but splits into two abbreviations; in this down clue 'underneath' puts the works below them.
explanation.definitionFit: Many windmills were built to drive pumps that lift groundwater or drain land, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stranger more than happy to be without central heating

indicators.note: being without something means it has been removed from the word

parts.note: more cheerful is more than merely happy
CH is the usual abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: Someone even weirder than a cheerful person, living in a house with no heating.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEERIER loses its opening CH to leave EERIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerier means more uncanny or weird, which is a comparative sense of stranger.

clue.text: Theatre school

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the name of several theatres, such as the one in London's West End
second meaning: Aristotle's school in Athens, and a word for a secondary school

explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'theatre school' it sounds like a drama college; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names famous playhouses and also the garden where Aristotle taught, hence any academy.

clue.text: Reflective device disturbed Yeats in church

indicators.note: something disturbed has been thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged
placing something in a place means it sits inside that word

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
the poet's name, rearranged

explanation.surface: A device that reflects how upset the poet Yeats was in church.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-eye is a glass reflector set into British road surfaces to mark lanes at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's-eyes are small reflectors set into roads that shine back in headlights, so they are a reflective device.

clue.text: Switch positions every now and then

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the two settings of a switch
second meaning: intermittently, from time to time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a verb telling you to swap places, but it is the light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch has two settings, and the same phrase as an adverb means intermittently or occasionally.

clue.text: Butcher's tailless dog is dead

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is dropped, here from each of the next two words

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
taken as written
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A butcher's dog, its tail docked, has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' docks both the dog and the word 'is'. 'Butcher' is a verb here, not the shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher something is to hack it about savagely, which is what mutilating means.

clue.text: Quarter-back practised to get permit

indicators.note: going back means the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: north-east is one quarter of the compass
a practised person is able or skilled

explanation.surface: An American football quarterback trained in order to earn a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter-back' is the American football position, but it splits into a compass quarter written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to make something possible or allow it, a verb synonym of permit.

clue.text: Subtly kill sovereign in East Coast city

indicators.note: something placed in a city sits inside that city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York, on the US East Coast
ice is slang for kill
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L is the pound sign's letter

explanation.surface: A discreet assassination of a monarch in a city such as Boston or New York.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound, so it gives L. Both kill and pound go inside NY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicely can mean with fine precision or delicacy, so it matches subtly as an adverb.

clue.text: A fellow's smooth and rich

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow
fluent speech flows smoothly

explanation.surface: A chap who is suave and wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent describes people with plenty of money, a straightforward synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Maybe girlfriends dream fancifully about Irish sons

indicators.note: done fancifully means done with imagination, so the letters are freely rearranged
going about something means surrounding it

parts.note: the word rearranged
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Girlfriends perhaps have romantic fantasies about Irish boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dream' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is only the fodder; Irish sits inside its rearranged letters, not around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Girlfriends are one example of people who are fond of someone, hence the 'maybe' signalling an example.

clue.text: Crooked board member's involved in first-rate business deal

indicators.note: something involved in another thing is caught up inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
the king is a piece on a chessboard
an MBO is a management buyout

explanation.surface: A dodgy company director is mixed up in a top-class business transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board member' points to a company director but means a chess piece; 'Crooked' suggests a criminal but means bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms akimbo are bent at the elbow with hands on hips, so the word describes something crooked in shape.

clue.text: Void in space and time

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide
O looks like zero, nothing, a void

explanation.surface: An empty gap within the fabric of space-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space and time' reads as one physics phrase, but 'time' is the definition and 'and' just joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long period, so it is a stretch of time in the broad sense.

clue.text: Good lord follows drinks with game

parts.note: two spirits, gin and rum
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise like 'Good lord!'

explanation.surface: A nobleman arrives after the drinks, along with some entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the exclamation after the two drinks. 'Good lord' sounds like an aristocrat but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a two-player card game in the rummy family, so it is an instance of a game.

clue.text: Weapon turned up in seizure

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
the answer is sitting in the following word, inside its letters

parts.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A gun appears among items confiscated in a police raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun, a specific example of a firearm or weapon.

clue.text: Capital investment in medical assistance rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: MED is a short form of medical
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: Money put into health services has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital investment' sounds financial, but capital is the head and investment is what invests or adorns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a crown or jewelled band worn on the head, so it is something placed upon a head.

clue.text: Running off with online journal containing access code

indicators.note: one word containing another holds it within its letters

parts.note: an electronic log or diary kept on the web
a PIN is a personal identification number used to gain access

explanation.surface: Someone absconds with a web diary that holds a password.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping means fleeing secretly, usually to marry, so it is a form of running away.

clue.text: Dishonest scheme — it may require DIY?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crime arranged in advance, often with inside help
second meaning, read literally: a household task such as fixing shelves to a wall

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: read word by word, the phrase is a task of hanging things up, the sort of do-it-yourself work done at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a fraud prearranged to deceive, often an inside job staged to look genuine.

clue.text: Riders heading off after Pole and Scandinavians

indicators.note: with the head taken off, the first letter is lost

parts.note: N is the North Pole
people riding horses

explanation.surface: Horse riders setting out behind a Polish man and some Scandinavians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the beheaded riders behind N. 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a geographical pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the people of ancient and medieval Scandinavia, especially the Vikings.

clue.text: Imaginatively take off year with undiminished energy

parts.note: a made-up word for removing clothing, the opposite of wear
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone takes a year out and comes back full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imaginatively' admits that UNWEAR is not a real word; it is not an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Unweary describes someone not tired, so it describes a person whose vigour is not reduced.

clue.text: Clash with a queen

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A confrontation with a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A war is an armed conflict, and a clash can mean a battle or conflict between forces.

clue.text: Checked sound of noisy shower?

indicators.note: the sound of something is how it is heard, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a heavy shower pounding indoors on a roof is rain that came down inside

explanation.surface: Someone checked what that loud noise from the bathroom shower was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' suggests a bathroom, but it is a rain shower, and 'noisy' points to the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse or a person is to restrain them, so reined in means checked or curbed.

clue.text: Picture with bottom of artist

parts.note: pic is short for picture
ass is American slang for the backside
o' is a shortened of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: A painting showing an artist's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' looks like a last-letter selection, but bottom is a whole word and 'of' supplies its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, so he is a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: Supporter of Thor Heyerdal?

parts.note: surface reading: a fan or backer of the Norwegian explorer
setter's reading: a roof beam, or a fellow traveller on a floating log craft like his Kon-Tiki

explanation.walkthrough: Thor Heyerdahl crossed the Pacific on a balsa-log craft, so anyone sharing his mode of travel fits; the word also means a beam that holds up a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sloping beam supporting a roof and someone who travels by raft, as the explorer did.

clue.text: A feather trimmed on American eagle

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the last letter is cut away

parts.note: taken as written
a quill is a large feather
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A feather clipped from a bald eagle, America's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'on' puts the A-plus-feather above American.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquila is Latin for eagle and is the name of a constellation known as the Eagle.

clue.text: Half finish a grid (cryptic) — that's unbecoming

indicators.note: something cryptic is enigmatic and puzzling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the first half of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver abandons a half-done cryptic grid, which seems a poor show.
explanation.walkthrough: Infra dig is short for Latin infra dignitatem, below one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something beneath one's dignity, which is what unbecoming conduct is.

clue.text: Honours seen in one hand in two

indicators.note: a thing in another is placed inside its letters

parts.note: a pair of hands, closed
R is right, one of the two hands

explanation.surface: Honours spotted, in card terms, in one player's hand out of two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' stands for two hands, picking up the clue's earlier hand. Honours and hand suggest card games but mean university degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Firsts are top-class university degrees in Britain, the highest grade of honours degree.

clue.text: I need a translated classical book

indicators.note: translated text is turned into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A student needs a translation of an ancient text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeneid is Virgil's Latin epic about Aeneas, a famous work of the classical world.

clue.text: Regularly search a pouch

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Routinely go through a bag or pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a baglike cavity in a plant or animal, so it is a natural pouch.

clue.text: Confusion follows American's agreement with up-and-coming businessman

parts.note: yup is American casual for yes
pie is printers' term for jumbled type, hence a muddle

explanation.surface: Muddle ensues when an American agrees with an ambitious young executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the confusion after the agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A yuppie is a young urban professional, an ambitious and rising person in business.

clue.text: Producer's resentment about return of a bishop

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
anger is resentment or wrath

explanation.surface: A record producer is bitter about a bishop coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: RR reads the same either way, so its return changes nothing; it follows A and precedes the resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: A music producer often works up the musical setting of a song, which is an arranger's job.

clue.text: Mistakes Bond's boss for Q's predecessor in Hollywood's output?

indicators.note: one thing for another means it takes the other's place

parts.note: M is James Bond's chief at MI6
P comes just before Q in the alphabet
film outtakes of fluffed scenes

explanation.surface: Bond films swapped M for Q, a mix-up in a Hollywood production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Q's predecessor' suggests the earlier gadget-master in the Bond films, but it is the letter before Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers is British informal for embarrassing blunders, so it is a synonym of mistakes.

clue.text: Group of three almost consuming four trifles

indicators.note: consuming something means taking it inside
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a triad is a set of three
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A trio nearly eating four desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: The four goes inside the shortened group after its first two letters, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are unimportant details or matters, which is what trifles in the plural mean.
